items.sentence: Her ______ reason for resigning from the firm was ill health, although several colleagues suspected that a prolonged quarrel with the board had been the real cause.
items.explanation: Ostensible means apparently true but not necessarily genuine, which fits the contrast with the real cause that colleagues suspected.

items.sentence: (A) ______ the housing scheme was launched with considerable fanfare in the capital last spring, its uptake in rural districts has been (B) ______, largely because most eligible families remain unaware that it exists.
items.explanation: Although sets up the contrast between a grand launch and weak take-up, and tepid is the result that the unawareness of families explains; the other pairs break either the logic or the sense.

items.sentence: The new lending policy was widely welcomed by economists as a sensible reform; ______, its implementation has been hampered by administrative delays and unclear guidelines at the branch level.
items.explanation: The second clause reverses the favourable reception, so a contrastive connector is needed; the other linkers add to the praise or present the delays as its result.

items.sentence: The auditor's report was ______ in its criticism of the management, naming every lapse in procedure and leaving the directors no room to claim that they had been unaware of the problems.
items.explanation: Unsparing criticism is severe and leaves nothing unmentioned, which matches the naming of every lapse; the other adjectives suggest mildness, doubt or a token effort.

items.sentence: A candidate's lack of (A) ______ with the subject can usually be (B) ______ by thorough preparation, a calm temperament and a logical approach to every unfamiliar question.
items.explanation: Familiarity takes the preposition with, and good preparation can offset a lack of it; the other pairs fail on collocation or give a verb that makes preparation harmful.

items.sentence: The manager's ______ attitude towards deadlines frustrated a team that had worked late every evening to meet them, since he treated them as optional and seldom completed his own tasks on time.
items.explanation: A cavalier attitude is careless and dismissive, which explains the team's frustration; the other adjectives describe careful behaviour that would not annoy hard-working colleagues.

items.sentence: Years of ______ spending, during which the council funded grand projects with borrowed money, left the municipality with a mountain of debt that it could not hope to repay from its modest revenues.
items.explanation: Profligate means recklessly extravagant, which explains why borrowing for grand projects ended in unmanageable debt; the other words describe careful saving.

items.sentence: Retail inflation turned out to be (A) ______ than analysts had feared for the quarter, which eased pressure on household budgets; (B) ______, the central bank saw no need to raise interest rates at its next policy review.
items.explanation: Milder inflation naturally removes the pressure for a rate rise, so a connector of consequence is needed; pairs with harsher inflation or a contrastive linker break that logic.

items.sentence: The professor's lecture on monetary policy was so ______ that even students with no background in economics could follow every step of her argument without difficulty.
items.explanation: Lucid means clear and easy to follow, as the result clause requires; the other words describe material that is obscure or hard to understand.

items.sentence: Coastal planners favour planting dense belts of mangroves along the shoreline because the trees can ______ the impact of storm surges on nearby fishing villages and farmland.
items.explanation: To mitigate is to lessen the severity of something, which is why planners favour the trees; the other verbs would increase or cause the damage.

items.sentence: The subsidy scheme was originally meant to (A) ______ the financial burden on small taxpayers, yet its tangled rules and repeated amendments only served to (B) ______ confusion among the very beneficiaries it targeted.
items.explanation: Easing the burden is the intended aim, and the word yet introduces the opposite outcome, so the rules compound confusion; the other pairs state an aim nobody would have or an outcome that would not be a failure.

items.sentence: Asked whether the merger talks had collapsed, the spokesperson gave an ______ reply that neither confirmed nor denied the persistent rumours circulating in the market.
items.explanation: Equivocal means deliberately vague or open to more than one reading, which matches a reply that neither confirms nor denies; the other adjectives describe clear, definite statements.

items.sentence: The report's central ______ that consumer demand would remain stable throughout the year proved unfounded once the festive season ended and household spending dropped sharply.
items.explanation: The noun assumption is needed after the adjective central and can be followed by a that-clause; the other forms are verb or adjective forms that cannot serve as the noun here.

items.sentence: Banks are expected to exercise (A) ______ in sanctioning loans to new borrowers, since careless appraisal can (B) ______ the quality of their asset portfolios over a period of several years.
items.explanation: Prudence is the quality expected in lending, and careless appraisal would erode portfolio quality; the other pairs combine a faulty quality or an improving verb with a context that rejects them.

items.sentence: The firm paid lip ______ to sustainability in its glossy annual report, yet it continued to discharge untreated waste into the river that flows past the village.
items.explanation: To pay lip service is a fixed idiom meaning to profess support without acting on it, which matches the firm's continued pollution; none of the other words forms that idiom.

items.sentence: Although automation promises to (A) ______ routine office tasks and free staff for creative work, experts caution that it may also (B) ______ the skills of the employees who currently perform them.
items.explanation: Streamline matches the promised benefit, and erode matches the cautionary note about workers' skills; the other pairs make the promise negative or the warning positive.

items.sentence: Government subsidies, however generous, tend to ______ rather than cure the structural weaknesses of an ailing industry, merely postponing the hard decisions that real reform requires.
items.explanation: Mask rather than cure contrasts hiding a problem with solving it, and the clause about postponed decisions confirms that the weaknesses are only hidden; the other verbs all mean to solve.

items.sentence: The tribunal's verdict was (A) ______ as a complete vindication of the company by those who had defended it, though its critics (B) ______ that the underlying questions remained unanswered.
items.explanation: Defenders would hail the verdict as a vindication, and critics, set against them by though, would argue that questions remained unanswered; in the other pairs one or both verbs make no sense in that context.
